The ZA Zb3 form is on a wine-storage jar, alongside VINa 32. A candidate gloss restricted to one named god or one sanctuary must explain this additional context. A general act such as providing, dedicating, or transferring is a possible semantic family, not a demonstrated meaning.

Sources: [IO Za6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwenge/lineara.xyz/master/commentary/IOZa6.html), [IO Za2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwenge/lineara.xyz/master/commentary/IOZa2.html), [PS Za2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwenge/lineara.xyz/master/commentary/PSZa2.html), [ZA Zb3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwenge/lineara.xyz/master/commentary/ZAZb3.html), [Monti](https://doi.org/10.1515/kadmos-2022-0005), [Thomas](https://doi.org/10.1515/kadmos-2020-0001).

There is prior scholarship for investigating an `-e` ending. Rose Thomas discusses that possibility in relation to the wine-jar text ZA Zb 3. This is credited as a conceptual precedent, not borrowed as a verified grammatical fact. The program ultimately tests the principal candidate using whole sign identities as well, so that its combinatorial prediction does not require exact Minoan pronunciations. [THOMAS](#src-thomas)

The newer AURA 15 volume was searched beyond the inherited word index. Davis explicitly prints the **A-KU-MI-NA / A-DU-KU-MI-NA / KU-MI-NA-QE** triple on p.47. The project must not claim discovery of that comparison. ZA Zb 3's coexistence of a wine notation and a ritual-formula-like sequence still permits a batch or ritual-event interpretation; it does not independently distinguish “give” from “dedicate” or identify recipients. Proposed ritual word order remains partly dependent on assumed sentence structure and sign interpretation. [AURA 15](https://epub.lib.uoa.gr/index.php/aura/article/view/2642), [targeted checks and competing source interpretations](notes/ritual_check.md).
